rationale: Genesis 19:37 names the older daughter's son Moab and states that 'He is the father of the Moabites of today.' The book of Ruth opens in 'the land of Moab' (Ruth 1:1), says Elimelech's sons 'took Moabite women as their wives, one named Orpah and the other named Ruth' (1:4), and calls her 'Ruth the Moabitess' (1:22; the title recurs at 2:2, 2:21, 4:5 and 4:10, five verses in all by a script count of the BSB, with 'the Moabitess' alone at 2:6). What this row tracks is a people named at its origin in Genesis and named again as the identity of Ruth; Ruth never names Lot or his daughters, which is why the type is motif and not explicit_reference. Graded strong because the recurrence is in the text of both books and named Jewish readers draw the line themselves: Genesis Rabbah 51:10 sets the conception of Moab beside Ruth 3:6 ('She went down to the threshing floor'), and the Talmud (Yevamot 77a) reads 'The lost article that was found among the daughters of Lot' as 'David and his royal house.' Matthew 1:5's naming of Ruth is the separate row conn-gen19-moab-matthew1, and Ruth 4:18-22 is already linked to Matthew in conn-matt1-genealogy-ruth4.
